correctness.rationale: Each edge value difference telescopes over positive adjacent valuation gaps. The edge count crossing a prefix of r ranked houses is \(r(N-r)-\sum_i x_i(n_i-x_i)\). For fixed r, the maximum within-part cross-cut pair count is the sum of the largest r marginal values \(n_i-2k-1\), each part’s marginal sequence being strictly decreasing. A single greedy priority sort achieves every prefix maximum simultaneously; strict positivity of all gaps makes this necessary for overall minimization. Ties occur at most once per part per level and can be ordered independently, yielding both enumeration formulas. Direct independent-objective exhaustive code ran successfully on 106 instances and 215126 assignment words; the proof establishes arbitrary N and gaps.

value.rationale: The mathematically motivated unanswered case of connected graphs with three or more complete communities admits a complete positive-gap-invariant optimizer classification and exact factorial count for every unequal size profile, extending the established bipartite classification. Unlike prior scalar path-wirelength formulas, the structure supports exact selection and sampling among all optimal allocations. This is an infinite graph class and arbitrary strictly increasing value vectors, not a narrow recomputation.
